newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas extends gains on weather, futures.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas extends gains on weather, futures.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices moved higher Thursday as cooler, stormy weather was forecast to bombard the East Friday and natgas futures rallied, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast gas prices rose another four cents to $2.01-2.06, with Transco (Station 65) quoted at $2.10-2.13.
Henry Hub prices were mostly at $2.07-2.08 per mmBtu, in line with May Henry Hub natgas futures, which were up 7.5 cents at $2.08 at 1342 EDT.
Similarly in south Texas, prices climbed seven cents to about $2 despite a return of seasonable weather to the region.

At the New York city-gate, prices gained another five to 10 cents to the mid-to-high $2.40s. Milder weather forecast to return to the Northeast early next week may temper demand in the next few days, market sources said.
Meanwhile, Appalachian prices were up an average of six cents to $2.27-2.33 on Columbia and mid-to-high-$2.30s on CNG.
In the Midcontinent, buyers for the most part ignored storage injections and entered the spot market in full force today. As a result, prices jumped six cents to the low-$1.90s.
However, Demarcation prices were little changed in the low-$1.90s, while Chicago city-gate prices soared to about $2.13-2.15, up about 10 cents from Wednesday.

Further west, Permian basin prices were up five cents in the low-to-mid $1.90s, while Waha values were quoted at $1.95-1.96. At the southern California border, prices were equally firmer in the low-$2 area.
American Gas Association data showed gas stocks fell 16 bcf last week to 836 bcf, or 26 percent of capacity. U.S. stocks were 290 bcf ahead of year-ago tallies.
